subject: Counter / fact-check of Dhruv Rathee podcast with ex-CEC S.Y. Quraishi (youtube.com/watch?v=foEYL-ElhTc, uploaded 2026-10-22)

facts.claim: ECI: 95.40 crore electors scrutinised in three SIR phases; 13.39 crore put in ASDD (absent/shifted/dead/duplicate) and other categories; eligible people can re-enrol
Of ~13 crore excluded: >71% (~9.5 cr) absent/shifted/others, ~2.7 cr dead, ~1.01 cr duplicate
Surjit Bhalla: deletions alone cannot establish mass disenfranchisement; 'starting point for scrutiny'; 73 million (one in four) aged 18-29 were not registered at 2024 Lok Sabha polls

RP Act 1950 s.21(3): ECI may at any time, for reasons recorded, direct a special revision of the roll for any constituency or part of a constituency, in such manner as it thinks fit. RER 1960 r.25: revision 'intensively or summarily or partly intensively and partly summarily'
facts.note: Quote from India Code on screen if possible. Quraishi said 'Section 23(3)' at 8:05 in the podcast; correct is 21(3). The phrase 'Special Intensive Revision' itself is not in the Act or Rules (true).

facts.claim: Supreme Court, 27 May 2026 (CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi): ECI empowered under Art 324 and s.21(3) to conduct SIR; deletion from roll is not a declaration of non-citizenship
facts.note: Full 124-page judgment text not read; based on news reports.

facts.claim: Bihar: 21.53 lakh new electors added after draft roll, 3.66 lakh removed (net +17.87 lakh); final roll 7.42 crore vs 7.89 crore before
Uttarakhand SIR: 4,01,276 new voters added, 17,05,130 removed
UP: 88 lakh Form 6 applications received during SIR; the '16.18 lakh mystery voters' report was rejected by UP CEO Navdeep Rinwa as pre-draft Form 6 forms collected door to door
facts.note: Contested: Reporters' Collective vs CEO. Present both.

facts.claim: Phase III not complete: Karnataka final roll due 27 Oct 2026, Maharashtra 4 Nov 2026
ECI never published a count of foreigners found in Bihar SIR
Newslaundry analysis: ~9,500 declared ineligible in Bihar final roll (0.012% of 7.42 cr), >85% in four Nepal-border districts
Quraishi's '500 foreigners (150 Bangladeshi, 350 Nepali women)' in Bihar
facts.note: He says he read it 'in some newspaper' (45:24). No source located.

facts.claim: Oct 2025: ECI counsel told SC no excluded Bihar voter had filed an appeal or complaint
Bihar 2025 assembly polls: 66.91% turnout (provisional), highest since 1951; women 71.6% vs men 62.8%
SC on 13 Apr 2026 refused interim voting rights to 34 lakh+ deleted West Bengal voters; plea 'premature', go to appellate tribunals
West Bengal 2026 result: BJP 208, AITC 80 of 294
WB appeals: ~37 lakh of 38 lakh appeals pending on 18 Sep 2026; ECI estimated tribunals may take 12 years
facts.note: Concede this. Quraishi said 21 years; ECI's own estimate is 12.

facts.claim: Scroll: in half the seats BJP won in Bengal, total SIR deletions exceed victory margin
facts.note: Critics' strongest point; expect it in comments. Deletions > margin does not show deleted people were eligible or would have voted one way.

facts.claim: Quraishi: '49-50 booths had 80-90% Muslims deleted'; a judge said 'vote next time'; SC asked whether to re-poll
facts.note: No public record found. Script asks viewers for the order copy.

facts.claim: Assam NRC final list excluded 19,06,657; no official religion-wise breakdown; Assam minister said govt had no such data
Unofficial leaked figures (unnamed IB sources): ~6.9 lakh Bengali Hindus, ~4.86 lakh Muslims among NRC excluded
facts.note: Only to show Quraishi's 12 lakh / 7 lakh split matches no known figure. Say 'unverified leak' on screen.

facts.claim: Delhi HC: fear of false declaration in using Form 6 after SIR exclusion is 'misplaced' since direction came from ECI
ECI reverted Form 6 to original format amid row; extra declaration restricted to SIR states
Rule 93(2)(a) Conduct of Election Rules: P&H HC order 9 Dec 2024 (Mehmood Pracha, Haryana polls); ECI letter to Law Ministry 17 Dec; amendment notified 10.23 pm 20 Dec 2024
facts.note: The Wire dates HC order 10 Dec. Either way ~11 days, not '2 hours'. Concede Law Ministry cleared it in <2 days.

facts.claim: Lavasa 2019: IT notice to wife Novel Singhal Lavasa over directorships; notices to sister; IT survey of son Abir's company Nourish Foods
Lavasa resigned as EC in Aug 2020 to join ADB as Vice-President (appointed mid-July 2020)
Section 16, CEC & ECs Act 2023: no civil/criminal proceedings against a person who is or was CEC/EC for acts done in discharge of official duty
SC remark 6 Oct 2026: election commissioners enjoy greater legal immunity than judges; ADR challenge pending
Indian Express 23 Sep 2026: ECs Sandhu and Joshi objected in writing at least 14 times in ~10 months
ECI 23 Sep 2026: all decisions incl. SIR taken unanimously; 26 Sep: commission adopted nine decisions (mandatory meetings/agendas, ECINET review)
SC 5 Oct 2026 refused interim order to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar; issued notice to ECI
Dhruv intro: 10 Oct Delhi internet shut, 7000+ detained incl. himself
facts.note: Mobile internet suspension in parts of Delhi and his detention are reported. Detention counts vary (~200 per Reuters police source, 500+, 10,000 nationwide). Not used in script.
